chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding

four who testified upon a married man with the adultery. Then one of them retracted after the man had been killed. He said: If the fourth one says, 'I was delusional', he would be struck the legal penalty, and fined the wergild. And if he says, 'I was deliberate', he would be killed.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference in legal ruling when a witness retracts testimony due to doubt versus deliberate intent in cases of adultery?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi details the judicial procedure for retracting testimony in the case of a muhsan (married man) convicted of zina, highlighting the critical distinction between doubt (shakk) and deliberate intent (ta'ammud) in determining whether the witness faces corporal punishment or execution. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on the precision of witness testimony and the corresponding financial (diya) and physical liabilities, rooted in the principle of qisas (retaliation) for bloodshed.
